responses.biography: Dr. Hesham Hussein, PhD, is an archaeologist, Egyptologist, and archaeological heritage specialist with over 25 years of professional experience in archaeological fieldwork, Egyptian frontier archaeology, excavation, epigraphy, rock inscriptions, digital heritage documentation, and heritage management. He currently serves as Undersecretary for Lower Egypt and Sinai Archaeology at the Supreme Council of Antiquities, Ministry of Tourism and Antiquities, Egypt. He earned his PhD in History and Civilization from Suez Canal University (2013). His research spans the Ways of Horus military fortresses, ancient copper mining and metallurgy in Sinai (Wadi el-Nasab), Hellenistic and Roman Pelusium (Temple of Zeus Kasios), rock art documentation (Al-Zolma/Al-Dalma rockshelter), and 3D photogrammetric digital archaeology.

responses.biography: Dr. Furqan Tahir is an environmental engineer and researcher at King Abdullah University of Science and Technology (KAUST) in the Environmental Science and Engineering program. He earned his Ph.D. in Sustainable Energy from Hamad Bin Khalifa University (HBKU), Qatar. His research expertise spans Life Cycle Assessment (LCA), environmental sustainability of desalination processes, the water-energy nexus, and systems-level decarbonization strategies.

responses.biography:
Dr. Celeste Chamberland, Ph.D., is a Professor of History and Program Director for the History and International Studies Programs at Roosevelt University in Chicago. She is a scholar of the history of medicine, early modern Europe, and the Atlantic world, with a specialized emphasis on gender, race, and cultural history.

Dr. Chamberland’s published research focuses on gender and the professionalization of surgery, as well as the history of mental illness in the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries. Her current research interests explore the relationship between masculinity, medical moralizing, and the proto-medicalization of addiction within the context of emergent global capitalism. She teaches courses spanning world history, the history of public health, medical racism, drugs in world history, epidemics, and gender and power in the Atlantic world.

Dr. Chamberland earned her Ph.D. in History from the University of California, Davis, her M.A. from Concordia University in Montreal, and her B.A. from the University of New Brunswick. Her research has been widely published in leading journals such as Social History of Medicine, History of Education Quarterly, Sixteenth Century Journal, and Journal of the History of Medicine and Allied Sciences.

responses.biography:
Dr. Ahmed Magdy Rabea, M.D., Ph.D., is an Assistant Professor of Medical Oncology & Hematology at the National Cancer Institute (NCI), Cairo University, and Consultant & Head of the Department of Medical Oncology at Shifa Hospital, New Cairo, Egypt. With over 20 years of clinical, translational research, and academic teaching experience across premier cancer centers in Egypt and Canada, Dr. Rabea provides comprehensive multidisciplinary care and clinical leadership with specialized expertise in thoracic oncology, breast cancer, prostate malignancies, and malignant hematology.

Dr. Rabea completed his Doctorate (Ph.D.) in Medical Oncology (2015) and Master of Science in Medical Oncology (2009) at the National Cancer Institute, Cairo University, following his MBBCh with Excellent with Honors from Kasr El Ainy Faculty of Medicine, Cairo University (2004). He subsequently completed advanced international training, including a Clinical Fellowship in Malignant Hematology and the Multiple Myeloma & Autologous Stem Cell Transplant Program at the Princess Margaret Cancer Centre, University of Toronto, Canada (2010), a Master of Advanced Oncology (M.Sc.) at Ulm University, Germany (2012), and European Society for Medical Oncology (ESMO) Board Certification (2012).

A dedicated clinical trialist and researcher, Dr. Rabea has served as Principal Investigator and Co-Investigator on numerous multinational Phase II–III clinical trials, including the KINDLE trial in stage III non-small cell lung cancer, the PARACHUTE study in renal cell carcinoma, and the FATIMA trial in HR+/HER2− metastatic breast cancer, as well as landmark studies in multiple myeloma, CML, and Castleman's disease. He has authored more than 30 peer-reviewed articles in leading oncology journals including Annals of Oncology, Journal of Cancer Education, Clinical Lymphoma Myeloma and Leukemia, JTO Clinical and Research Reports, and Blood.

Dr. Rabea actively serves in international oncology leadership, having served as Chair (2021–2023) and Deputy Chair (2020–2021) of the Career Development & Fellowships Committee for the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC), Abstract Reviewer for the World Lung Conference (WLC), and Coordinator for the Cairo ESMO Examination Session. He serves as Coordinator for the Egyptian Presidential Initiative for the Screening and Early Detection of Lung Cancer and actively drives cancer health-equity and guideline harmonization initiatives across the Middle East and Africa. In 2024, he was honored with the Best Oncologist in Egypt award by the FORTTUNA Awards.
